cues.text: I have an indoor camera hidden inside of this Airbnb and people are not happy about it.
So I made a video a couple days ago showing a guest breaking into the locked basement at one of
our Airbnb properties. And I got a lot of comments from people who were upset that I had a hidden
camera inside of the house. So Airbnb just released a new rule a couple days ago stating that effective
April 30th hosts are no longer allowed to have indoor security cameras anywhere in the property.
Now some of the properties that I have listed on Airbnb are century old homes where the basement
is very undesirable. So we use it as an owner's closet, cleaning closet, overflow stuff like that.
So we lock the door leading to the basement. I have it clearly stated on my listing description
on Airbnb that guests are not allowed to have access to the basement that it is locked off.
This is a special section on the Airbnb listing called guest access. So you know exactly where you
are and are not allowed to go. The basement is not part of the rented listing. You are not
renting the basement. So according to the Airbnb rules, you are not allowed to have cameras inside
of the property. But this is not part of the property because you are not renting that.
And because it is not an indoor space that is monitoring guests, it is in a locked space
that is not part of the listing. I have every right to monitor that space with a security camera.
